title: I challenged myself to build the core of a game in 72 hours.  I flipped things around - gave Fable control, and told it to treat me as a consultant.
author: JordanRunsForFun
selftext:
**AI-led for 72 hours, with a head start. What that looked like.**

**The head start:** two earlier projects of mine, EleventhRealm (a Godot survival game, all art in code) and WristForge (a Swift engine for the Apple Watch). The agents could read them and never write to them. Job one was to survey both and design a new engine from what held up, and to design out what didn't: Realm had no client prediction and no momentum, so you couldn't drive a car in it.

**The rules I set:** the AI leads and makes every choice. I'm a consultant it asks through a question queue on my phone. Nothing is done without an automated check, as a rule, with continuous integration testing before every commit.

**What the lead (Claude - Fable 5.2, mostly on xhigh) did with that:**

* Wrote the plan and a decisions log with a reason for every choice, and rewrote a state file at every stop, so a session cut off by a usage limit lost nothing.
* Wrote about 100 briefs, each naming the files a worker owns, what it may call and the check it must add, and ran up to four workers in parallel git worktrees.
* Merged only on green: 219 checks headless, a second suite on another PC, real GPU frames from Linux VMs.
* **Everything Measured instead of guessing.** The browser build ran at 3 to 15 frames a second on my iPhone, so it profiled why and had a native iPhone app on my phone the same afternoon. A rule that "a well-armed person on foot can stop a car" is held by computer players fighting 100 duels.

**The result:** Eleventh Street, a top-down city crime game with momentum driving, police, explosions and a 16-player battle royale. 870 commits, about 150k lines. 

It's really just a start. A strong core. A foundation for a competitive and fun shooter that can be played on any device. 

Trailer: [https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=RqhS3C\_fKPo](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=RqhS3C_fKPo)

Early-tester sign-up: [https://street.realm11.ca](https://street.realm11.ca)

Happy to answer questions about the setup in the comments: the briefs, the checks, what went wrong, what I'd do differently.

replies.author: JordanRunsForFun
replies.body: That is certainly a huge part of the inspiration, yes.

comments.author: freqCake
comments.body: Do you think the result is fun?

replies.author: JordanRunsForFun
replies.body:
That’s always the real goal isn’t it?

So far, as I’m a bit of a car enthusiast myself, I have spent a lot of time tuning  the cars.. My goal is to start with that because it’s something I’m pretty good at and have a solid understanding of what I’m after. (for example all the cars are based on real cars with a real drivetrain and there is a difference between a front wheel drive car and a rear wheel drive car and an all-wheel-drive car and there’s a difference between an open differential and a limited slip differential that will make higher performance cars rewarding to own in the game. 

I’m leaning on some friends to help me balance the shooting parts. Shooter games are fun to me, but are certainly outside of my area of expertise.  

Finally, I’m writing the stories myself for the single player campaign and using Claude to help me storyboard and write various threads so that it’s sort of deep and interesting while at the same time, not taking itself too seriously and not sounding like it was written by AI  

But at the end of the day, you are 100% right. Fun is the real goal and it’s way harder than a shiny demo.

comments.author: Famous_Ad_5611
comments.body:
Hey, listen.. I love GTA 1 and 2. And over the past few months, I've been making my own versions of the game using AI so I kind of get your vibe (all of mine were shit xD) - so let me help you out a little bit here.

I don't know much about the game itself, but the trailer is something we AI folks (and I'm guilty of this too) seem to struggle with.

We show mechanics, we show how similar our games are to something else to evoke nostalgia (i'ts mostly a fault of ai writing script for trailer xD). But hey - show your game. Don't put it through the lens of trying to compare it to other games.

Check out this anniversary trailer for GTA 3: [https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=agACYOeuX7k](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=agACYOeuX7k)

See something there? Or rather, notice what's missing? There are no text overlays explaining what you can do in the game. And yet, everything you can do is shown. Driving cars, making jumps, shooting people, interacting with the world, and experiencing a great story...

There should be more to your game than just being a clone. But if it really is just a clone with 10 basci missions and 20 random cars... well, then it's just a clone.

Because here's the thing - AI can almost eliminate the coding part of game development. But it can't full eliminatd all the other parts. Game design, storytelling, and marketing. ;D ... well not yet...
